name: Net Art Browser
summary: Art made inside the browser from raw HTML: default grey ground, blue links, Times text, broken frames and visible code. The net.art artists of the 1990s used the window as the canvas.

philosophy.core_thesis: The browser is the material: show its defaults, its errors and its source as the work itself.
design_principles: Keep the browser defaults: Times text at 16px, blue links (#0000EE), visited links (#551A8B) and a margin of 8px.
Choose one ground: white (#FFFFFF), default grey (#C0C0C0) or black with green text (#00FF00).
Split the window with nested frames at 1px borders, and let one frame show an error or the raw source.
Set text as plain lines of 60 to 80 characters; use no images, or use 1 stretched GIF.
Make links the only navigation; name them with single words or with the URL itself.
Show the code: print a block of HTML, a status line or an error message as visible content.
Let colour and size glitch: one line in 72px bold red (#FF0000) among 16px black text.
anti_patterns: Soft shadows, gradients and rounded cards

layout.grid_mechanics: A single flowing column that fills the window; frames split it at 50% or 33% with visible 1px borders.
layout.whitespace_ratio: 60% to 90% of the page is empty ground; the spacing is the browser default of 8px and 16px.
layout.alignment_rules: Everything flush left and top; text wraps at the window edge with no max width.
layout.container_geometry: Raw rectangles with a 0px radius; frames and tables show their borders at 1px.

font_pairings.note: Tinos is the open look-alike of Times, the default browser face.
Arimo is the open look-alike of Arial; Courier Prime serves the code and the log lines.
A mono display over default text.

hierarchy_rules: Use 16px for body text and 32px bold for a single heading.
Use underline and colour for links and nothing else for emphasis.
Use bold and italic as the only weights.

color.palette_structure: The default web colours: white or grey ground, black text, blue and purple links, one pure accent.
color.contrast_rules: Black on white is 21:1; link blue on white is 8:1; green on black is 15:1; red is for lines of 24px or more.
color.surface_treatment: Flat colour with no gradient; the window background colour is the only surface.
color.light_and_shadow: No light and no shadow; borders are 1px solid lines or the old 2px inset.

materiality.surface_simulation: The default browser page: no skin, no material.
materiality.border_rules: A 1px solid black line on frames and tables; a 2px inset line only on form fields.

ornamentation_details.iconography: No icon set; use text links, the broken-image mark and the 16px favicon default.
ornamentation_details.illustration: No illustration; use the code, a stretched 1px GIF, a table of random numbers or a screenshot of an error dialog.

motion.transition_physics: Pages change with a hard cut on each click; one meta refresh at 5s replaces the page; no easing.
motion.hover_and_active: Hover shows the default pointer and the link target in the status bar; the active link turns red (#FF0000).

emotion.target_response: The viewer feels unsure whether the page is broken or planned, and then sees the idea.

use_cases: art project pages and festival sites
avoid_when: The page must sell a product.
The audience needs clear and friendly navigation.
The brand needs trust and polish.

modifiers.how: Add a tiled background, a counter and an under-construction sign.
Keep the empty ground and swap the defaults for one chosen type face.
Move to a black text grid with 16 ANSI colours.

pack.why: Plain square pixel marks keep the raw, unstyled feel of default HTML.

ground.why: The ground is the bare browser window with no pattern.

tailwind.classes: rounded-none border border-black bg-[#C0C0C0] px-2 py-0.5 text-base
